Title: A colored-comb basis for the full weighted partition poset
Original question and proposer: Rafael S. González D’León (Conjecture 5.11. Also Conjecture 6.3.4 of the 2014 dissertation)
Proposed result: The proposed combs form a basis for every number of colors. Decomposing a tree at its root gives exactly the number of classes required for independence.

Title: A descent-preserving injection for mixed caterpillar inequalities
Original question and proposer: Nathan R. T. Lesnevich and Peter R. W. McNamara (Section 7(3), equation (7.4))
Proposed result: A descent-preserving injection explains an inequality observed in the original paper. The proof extends it to side posets of arbitrary size whose largest label lies at a maximal element.

Title: Characteristic polynomials of multiweighted partitions
Original question and proposer: Rafael S. González D’León and Michelle L. Wachs (Question 7.1)
Proposed result: A Laguerre coefficient formula works for every size and number of colors above two. Odd ground-set size gives no real zero, even size gives one, and the absolute coefficients are strictly log-concave.

Title: Characters of the free Lie algebra with compatible brackets
Original question and proposer: Rafael S. González D’León (Question 7.13. Also Question 8.3.8 of the 2014 dissertation)
Proposed result: A finite multinomial sum gives the character on every cycle type and all irreducible multiplicities. Every prime-length cycle has trace −1 in each bracket multidegree.

Title: Deleting one edge from a join in the Kromatic symmetric function
Original question and proposer: Laura Pierson and Soham Samanta (Question 2.24, construction alternative)
Proposed result: One five-term expansion per graph certifies an infinite family of equal pairs. For joins with one edge removed, an exact vertex-deletion criterion decides when the endpoint can change.

Title: Equal power-sum coordinates beyond symmetric functions
Original question and proposer: Jean-Christophe Aval, Karimatou Djenabou and Peter R. W. McNamara (Section 5.2)
Proposed result: The two power-sum bases give identical coordinates for some nonsymmetric functions in every degree at least five. One linear condition describes all such coincidences on two-part compositions.

Title: Forbidden subposets for fair series-parallel orders
Original question and proposer: Doriann Albertin, Jean-Christophe Aval and Hugo Mlodecki (Remark 4.2)
Proposed result: Three forbidden patterns characterize the class under induced and convex containment. The proof also treats convex containment alone and the effect of allowing arbitrary cover deletions.

Title: Point deletion does not determine poset substitution
Original question and proposer: Thomas Browning, Max Hopkins and Zander Kelley (Conjecture 48 in the June 2016 manuscript) · 2017 preprint, Conjecture 4.11 · FPSAC 2018, Conjecture 4.7
Proposed result: Two posets agree before and after point deletion. Substituting two incomparable points gives 138 order-preserving maps to three colors on one side and 140 on the other.

Title: Reading longest chains from fundamental support
Original question and proposer: Peter R. W. McNamara and Ryan E. Ward (Question 4.4) and Nathan R. T. Lesnevich and Peter R. W. McNamara, 2020 (Question 3.8)
Proposed result: The fundamental support determines the height of every labeled poset and which strict and weak edge patterns occur as subsequences on its chains.

Title: Real zeros for a single lamination in a polygon
Original question and proposer: Wonwoo Kang, Kyeongjun Lee and Eunsung Lim (Conjecture 1, disk formulation in v4. The original 2025 preprint asked about a broader class of surfaces)
Proposed result: Every such polynomial has only negative real zeros and hence log-concave coefficients. The result holds for every triangulation, arc and single curve in an unpunctured disk.

Title: Recognizing a tree from its orientation functions
Original question and proposer: Jean-Christophe Aval, Karimatou Djenabou and Peter R. W. McNamara (Question 5.5, numbered 5.1 in the first preprint)
Proposed result: The set of highest-ascent coefficients over all orientations already determines the undirected tree. Multiplicities and all lower coefficients can be discarded.

Title: Reconstructing a labeled rooted tree from its partition enumerator
Original question and proposer: Jean-Christophe Aval, Karimatou Djenabou and Peter R. W. McNamara (Conjecture 1.3, first posted in 2022)
Proposed result: The partition enumerator recovers the root, the branches and every strict or weak edge. A rooted forest has a symmetric enumerator precisely when all its components are hooks.

Title: Series-parallel structure under labeled partition equivalence
Original question and proposer: Ricky Ini Liu and Michael Weselcouch (Question 5.4)
Proposed result: Two connected labeled posets can have equal enumerators even when only one is series-parallel. Grafting chains on two small forks gives an infinite family of such pairs.

Title: Strict interlacing in consecutive ranks for type-D Eulerian polynomials
Original question and proposer: Chak-On Chow (§5)
Proposed result: For every $q>0$, the zeros at consecutive ranks strictly interlace from rank three onward.

Title: Substring composition and switching of integer compositions
Original question and proposer: José Aliste-Prieto, Jeremy L. Martin, Jennifer D. Wagner and José Zamora (Section 7.3, Question 1)
Proposed result: Equality of ζ is equivalent to equality of substring-composition multisets of the binary cut words. Two compositions of 24 have equal ζ and different coarsening polynomials.

Title: The excedance polynomials of parking functions are not always real-rooted
Original question and proposer: Per Alexandersson
Proposed result: An exact integer inequality certifies a nonreal root at size 17, settling the all-sizes conjecture. The coefficient formula applies at every size.

Title: The first correction to the large-genus roots of deformed monotone Hurwitz polynomials
Original question and proposer: Xavier Coulter, Norman Do and Ellena Moskovsky (Conj. 3.15)
Proposed result: For every fixed cycle profile, the first correction gives the direction and exponential rate at which each moving root approaches its limit.

Title: Unequal rowmotion averages on a uniform fence
Original question and proposer: Sergi Elizalde, Matthew Plante, Tom Roby and Bruce E. Sagan (Conjecture 6.4(b) in v1, later Conjecture 5.4(b))
Proposed result: On a 32-element fence one 237-step orbit has total ideal size 3,774. The proposed half-size average would give 3,792.

Title: Universal Schur coefficients of chromatic symmetric functions
Original question and proposer: Noah Kravitz (Section 1.2, final paragraph)
Proposed result: Exactly the hook shapes have nonnegative coefficients for every graph. For each other shape, a complete multipartite graph makes that specific coefficient negative.

Title: Which threshold-labeled posets are quasisymmetric?
Original question and proposer: Thomas Lam and Pavlo Pylyavskyy (Problem 7.1)
Proposed result: Every nonzero quasisymmetric output reduces to strict, weak and deleted edges. Finite forbidden patterns characterize the labelings. General computable thresholds give an undecidable recognition problem.

Title: An exponential gap in the Lazy Beaver runtime spectrum
Original question and proposer: Scott Aaronson (Conj. 25)
Proposed result: Even when a machine is tested on every initial tape, the number of distinct runtime profiles is exponentially smaller than the number of graphically accessible transition tables. This is a stronger bound than the one needed to refute the original conjecture.

Title: Constant advice between successive prefix-free Busy Beaver records
Original question and proposer: Scott Aaronson (§5.5). Dan Brumleve posed the separate bit-extraction suggestion in 2017
Proposed result: For optimal prefix-free programs, constant advice suffices at every length. In the classical state-count model the one-step cost averages $\Theta(\log N)$ below $N$ states.

Title: Countable orders of strong settling times
Original question and proposer: Barbara F. Csima and Richard A. Shore (Conj. 7.16 in the 2006 manuscript, published in 2007)
Proposed result: Every countable partial order has a representation by computably enumerable sets ordered both by strong settling-time domination and by Turing reducibility. The entire family can lie strictly below the halting problem.

Title: Exact oracle bounds for memoryless language generation
Original question and proposer: Jon Kleinberg, Anay Mehrotra, Amin Saberi and Grigoris Velegkas (§6, oracle-access question, applied to Theorem 3.1)
Proposed result: When examples may repeat arbitrarily, the exact universal oracle for memoryless set-valued generation is the first Turing jump for decidable presentations and the second for enumerable ones. The thresholds hold for every fixed sliding window.

Title: Language inclusion for Busy Beaver bouncer tapes
Original question and proposer: Tristan Stérin (original post). Justin Blanchard proposed the restrictions tested here
Proposed result: An exact linear-time inclusion test for aligned tape formulas with separated repeaters and equal repeater counts. An empty-wall counterexample separates two proposed conditions.

Title: Splitting the Busy Beaver runtime
Original question and proposer: Toby Ord (original question). Scott Aaronson gave the upper-bound formulation in the same discussion
Proposed result: The pointwise maximum of two runtime records is Busy Beaver. Each record eventually outgrows every computable function. An oracle for either record cannot compute an upper bound for the other.

Title: Which dictionaries hit all sufficiently zero-padded binary words?
Original question and proposer: Bogdan Alecu, Maria Chudnovsky, Sepehr Hajebi and Sophie Spirkl (Question 1.11 in v1, later Question 8.3)
Proposed result: A bounded-zero-run subdictionary criterion characterizes padded unavoidability. Recognition is decidable for regular dictionaries, Σ⁰₂-complete for primitive recursive indices and Σ⁰₃-complete for enumerable indices.

Title: A communication obstruction to optimal noise rates in conditional disclosure of secrets
Original question and proposer: Zhou Li, Siyan Qin, Xiang Zhang, Jihao Fan, Haiqiang Chen and Giuseppe Caire (§VIII, achievability of the linear converse in Theorem 2 (full version of the ISIT 2025 work))
Proposed result: The graph bound can strictly exceed the best possible linear noise rate. On the Li–Sun graph it gives 4/7, while every linear scheme has rate at most 14/25. An entropy argument relates noise to communication along every unqualified path and applies to nonlinear messages as well.

Title: A projective shuffle for private majority and three-party predicates
Original question and proposer: Shizuru Iino, Shota Ikeda, Kazumasa Shinagawa, Yang Li, Kazuo Sakiyama and Daiki Miyahara (§4, second open problem (CANS 2025))
Proposed result: One uniform permutation from a 60-element group suffices. Turning over all six cards reveals exactly the majority bit. Over larger projective lines, the same construction realizes precisely the three-party predicates expressible as an XOR of pairwise terms, with one marked point per sender.

Title: Classifying ideal private simultaneous messages on prime alphabets
Original question and proposer: Keitaro Hiwatashi and Reo Eriguchi (§5.2, tightness of the prime-alphabet bound in Theorem 8 (ITCS 2026))
Proposed result: Gives the complete list and exact count of connected nondegenerate ideal PSM functions for every prime alphabet. The functions come from affine differences, point–hyperplane incidence in projective spaces, and one exceptional table on eleven symbols. For arbitrary finite alphabet size, a Latin square admits ideal PSM exactly when it is a relabelled group table.

Title: Corrector orders of weightwise almost perfectly balanced Boolean functions
Original question and proposer: Martin Grenouilloux, Chunlei Li and Pierrick Méaux (Conjecture 1, the nonexistence clause for correctors)
Proposed result: For any fixed positive excess, a set of dimensions of natural density one admits weightwise almost perfectly balanced functions whose corrector order exceeds the conjectured bound by exactly that amount.

Title: Malicious-verifier statistical zero knowledge for proofs of proximity
Original question and proposer: Itay Berman, Ron D. Rothblum and Vinod Vaikuntanathan (§1.1, footnote 7 in the 2017 preprint (footnote 10 at ITCS 2018))
Proposed result: In the polylogarithmic regime, honest-verifier statistical proofs of proximity admit statistical simulation against arbitrary verifier strategies. The transformation applies to the original graph expansion and bipartiteness promises and keeps verification polynomial in log input length, security parameter and inverse proximity.

Title: Nonlinearity of a cyclic weightwise quadratic Boolean function
Original question and proposer: Pierrick Méaux and Yassine Ozaim (§6.3, the formula for the family u in dimensions divisible by four)
Proposed result: The proposed nonlinearity formula for u fails at every multiple of four from 24 onward. An explicit Walsh coefficient gives a gap of at least 16ℓ − 88 in dimension 4ℓ, and the maximum Walsh magnitude has exponential growth rate 3/4 on a base-two logarithmic scale per variable.

Title: Private simultaneous messages with one bit of evaluator memory
Original question and proposer: Akinori Kawachi and Yuto Nishikubo (§1.3, the classical one-bit evaluator comparison in the input-controlled gate model of §2.1)
Proposed result: A Boolean output admits exact, perfectly private simultaneous messages with a one-bit evaluator precisely when fixing one designated party’s input makes every slice an XOR of single-party functions. For three or more single-bit senders, the only symmetric examples are parity, its complement and the two constants.

Title: Recognizing the network condition for granular synchrony
Original question and proposer: Wentao Li formulated the question. Giridharan, Abraham, Crooks, Nayak and Ren gave the graph condition in 2024. Appan, Heath and Ren, 2025 established its application to secure computation.
Proposed result: Checking the network condition for secure multiparty computation is coNP-complete for every fixed rational fault fraction in [1/3, 1/2), even when the synchronous-link graph consists of two cliques with arbitrary links between them.

Title: Shared binary lookups with affine output decoding
Original question and proposer: Wentao Li formulated the question. David Heath, Vladimir Kolesnikov and Lucien Ng studied garbled lookup tables in 2024.
Proposed result: XORs and constants attain the minimum shared lookup width when each output is specified on at most three addresses. A gap first appears at four. For every fixed maximum number of specified addresses, the draft gives a sharp leading bound on worst-case width.

Title: The exact cost of affine joins in a bank of arithmetic switches
Original question and proposer: Wentao Li formulated the question. David Heath introduced arithmetic switches and the join-width cost in 2024.
Proposed result: For a fixed bank of equal-width arithmetic switches, the chromatic number of the graph of allowed simultaneous openings determines the exact cost of affine joins. A weighted coloring formula gives the optimum for mixed widths in an additive model.

Title: The failure probability of granular synchrony on random networks
Original question and proposer: Wentao Li formulated the question. Appan, Heath and Ren, 2025 established the secure-computation criterion studied here under random link assignments.
Proposed result: With independent synchronous links, a linear honest-set threshold and minimum link probability well above log(n)/n, a typical failing network has a unique separating partition. Its expected number of separating partitions gives the failure probability to vanishing relative error.

Title: When does uniqueness force a cyclic circuit to settle?
Original question and proposer: Wentao Li formulated the wiring question from David Heath’s 2023 cyclic-circuit model, §4, Definition 4.
Proposed result: A three-gate XOR circuit has a unique wire assignment but never settles. The draft characterizes exactly which wiring diagrams guarantee that a unique solution can be evaluated gate by gate.

Title: A proper permutation class without a first-order convergence law
Original question and proposer: Samuel Braunfeld and Matthew Kukla (Q5.4)
Proposed result: In a proper hereditary permutation class, the probability that the two orders share a least element tends to one along selected sizes and to zero at the immediately following sizes.

Title: A sum-closed permutation class without a logical limit law
Original question and proposer: Samuel Braunfeld and Matthew Kukla (Question 5.3)
Proposed result: Even when two permutations can always be joined by direct sum, the probability that the first entry is the minimum can fail to converge.

Title: A universal spectrum on uncoloured planar graphs
Original question and proposer: Arnaud Durand, Neil D. Jones, Johann A. Makowsky and Malika More (Q24 in the preprint, Q19 in the 2012 journal version)
Proposed result: A single first-order sentence about connected planar graphs of maximum degree three can represent every first-order spectrum. The reduction uses only equality on the input set.

Title: A zero-one law for two-connected graphs
Original question and proposer: Peter Heinig, Tobias Müller, Marc Noy and Anusch Taraz (two-connected question in §6)
Proposed result: For uniform labelled two-connected graphs in a proper 2-addable minor-closed class containing a cycle, every monadic second-order sentence converges exponentially to probability zero or one. The almost-sure theory is decidable exactly when the class has bounded treewidth.

Title: Logical limit laws and their probability spectrum for labeled compositions
Original question and proposer: Samuel Braunfeld and Matthew Kukla (Q5.1)
Proposed result: On uniform labelled compositions, every monadic second-order sentence has an exponentially convergent probability. First-order sentences already attain the full set of limits.

Title: Monadic second-order convergence for caterpillar forests
Original question and proposer: Peter Heinig, Tobias Müller, Marc Noy and Anusch Taraz (§6, the caterpillar-forest prediction immediately before Conjecture 6.3)
Proposed result: Every monadic second-order sentence has a limiting probability in a uniform labelled forest of caterpillars. A component-count criterion extends the result to smooth definable forest classes within bounded distance of paths.

Title: Three gaps in logical limit laws for random graphs
Original question and proposer: Peter Heinig, Tobias Müller, Marc Noy and Anusch Taraz (Conj. 6.2)
Proposed result: In every proper addable minor-closed graph class, at least three gaps separate the attainable limiting probabilities. Forests attain the sharp generating-function bound.

Title: Which slow sequences count labelled finite models?
Original question and proposer: Arnaud Durand, Neil D. Jones, Johann A. Makowsky and Malika More (converse and prime example following Q10)
Proposed result: The sequence of primes cannot enumerate the labelled model counts of a sentence in a fixed finite relational language. Counts bounded by a fixed exponential eventually have an exact exponential-polynomial formula for both first-order and monadic second-order sentences.

Title: Can a Bell colouring graph detect a surplus colour?
Original question and proposer: Brian Hearn (Section 1, first question preceding Conjecture 1.6)
Proposed result: For every palette of size at least two, the same Bell graph can arise at the chromatic number and with a spare colour. The ambiguity can persist even when both graph order and palette are given.

Title: Clique-cover degeneracy of map graphs on surfaces
Original question and proposer: Clément Dallard, Martin Milanič, Andrea Munaro and Shizhou Yang (Q7.3)
Proposed result: The worst-case clique-cover degeneracy on a surface of Euler genus $g$ grows as $\Theta(1+\sqrt{g})$.

Title: Different trees with the same joint subtree polynomial
Original question and proposer: José Aliste-Prieto, Jeremy L. Martin, Jennifer D. Wagner and José Zamora (Section 7.5, Question 2)
Proposed result: Two 23-vertex trees agree on the counts of all 14,532 subtrees by all three statistics. Adding the same positive number of pendant leaves at each vertex gives an infinite family.

Title: Equal chromatic square counts for trees with different degrees
Original question and proposer: Simon MacLean (Section 5, implication diagram)
Proposed result: Two trees have identical induced-square counts for every number of colours, but one has 15 leaves and the other has 16. Both proposed implications fail.

Title: Finite universal targets for tuple dicolouring
Original question and proposer: Gil Puig i Surroca (Chapter 7, Problem 7.14, thesis defended January 2026)
Proposed result: For k-tuple n-dicolouring a finite circular-homomorphism target exists exactly for k in {1, 2, n−1, n}. A finite acyclic-homomorphism target exists exactly for k in {1, n}.

Title: High-confidence graph reconstruction with maximal independent set queries
Original question and proposer: Lukas Michel and Alex Scott (Problem 5.2)
Proposed result: For inverse-polynomial failure the optimal nonadaptive query count is Θ(min{n², Δ² log n}) across all maximum degrees, ruling out the proposed improved bound.

Title: How many hosts are needed for simultaneous induced saturation of cographs?
Original question and proposer: Marthe Bonamy, Carla Groenland, Tom Johnston, Natasha Morrison and Alex Scott (§8, simultaneous hosts for finite cographs)
Proposed result: Countably infinitely many hosts are necessary and sufficient even for connected nontrivial cographs. Two explicit maximal families characterize which targets can share a host with the three-vertex path.

Title: How precisely must one measure resistance to recover every missing edge?
Original question and proposer: Huck Bennett, Mitchell Black, Amir Nayyeri and Evelyn Warton (ALT 2026, Sections 1.1 and 6.2–6.3)
Proposed result: One reading per missing pair permits exact polynomial-time recovery. For unweighted graphs the worst-case additive error radius has sharp leading term 1/n².

Title: Minimal domination in hereditary classes of incomparability graphs
Original question and proposer: Marthe Bonamy, Oscar Defrain, Piotr Micek and Lhouari Nourine (§7, Conjecture 7.3)
Proposed result: Forbidding any fixed induced co-bipartite graph gives an incremental-polynomial algorithm for minimal domination in incomparability graphs. Under ETH this exactly characterizes the tractable hereditary subclasses.

Title: One induced colouring-graph polynomial for each graph
Original question and proposer: Shamil Asgarli, Sara Krehbiel, Howard W. Levinson and Heather M. Russell (Section 6, discussion preceding the colouring-graph reconstruction conjectures)
Proposed result: For each finite simple graph G, a single connected test graph of polynomial size distinguishes G from every other graph. Two leading coefficients recover the order and edge count, and an induced embedding of the chosen test graph forces spanning containment.

Title: Path feedback arc sets in tournaments are NP-complete
Original question and proposer: Pierre Aboulker, Guillaume Aubian and Raul Lopes (2024 path question, numbered Problem 4.4 in the published version)
Proposed result: Deciding whether deleting the arcs of one undirected path makes a tournament acyclic is NP-complete, even given an ordering of backward degree at most two.

Title: Right-half-plane independence roots of random graphs
Original question and proposer: Jason I. Brown and Ben Cameron (Problem 2). Cameron posed the narrower-sector conjecture in 2019
Proposed result: For every fixed edge probability $0<p<1$, a root in the open right half-plane occurs with probability bounded away from zero along a subsequence. At $p=1/2$ the limit superior is at least $1-e^{-1/4}$.

Title: Rooted trees with identical random destruction data
Original question and proposer: Fabian Burghart (Conjecture 18 in v1, Conjecture 20 and the following question in the published version)
Proposed result: Two nonisomorphic 39-vertex rooted trees have the same trivariate polynomial and the same distribution of the number of vertices left at separation. The construction gives arbitrarily large examples.

Title: Unbounded fragments in unlabelled bridge-addable graph classes
Original question and proposer: Colin McDiarmid (Conjs. 3 and 4)
Proposed result: One bridge-addable class with finite exponential growth has nearly linear expected fragment size along a subsequence of graph orders. The same example contradicts both proposed bounds.

Title: An explicit joint run–return formula for rational Dyck paths
Original question and proposer: Lilan Dai, Shishuo Fu and Dun Qiu (§5)
Proposed result: A determinant formula counts paths with prescribed returns and either run statistic for every width at least the height.

Title: Equal-length Tamari orbits with unequal down-degree totals
Original question and proposer: Colin Defant and James Lin (Conjecture 10.2) · Sen-Peng Eu, Vei-Cheng Hioe and Yi-Lin Lee, 2026 (Conjecture 5.1, homometry assertion)
Proposed result: Two ordinary Tamari orbits of length 22 have down-degree totals 45 and 46. The same obstruction holds in all alternate Tamari lattices for the same boundary.

Title: The zeros of the Fuss–Dyck peak polynomials do not depend on the Fuss parameter
Original question and proposer: Per Alexandersson
Proposed result: Fixing the number of north steps and peaks fixes all zeros of the $NNE$ counting polynomial, with multiplicities, across all Fuss slopes.

Title: A depth-independent width for stable ReLU graph separation
Original question and proposer: Yair Davidson and Nadav Dym (Section 4.2 (ICLR 2025))
Proposed result: Width 2n+2 suffices at every fixed depth on graphs of at most n vertices. The expected output separation has a power-law lower bound in Tree Mover’s Distance.

Title: A finite generating list for shallow ReLU rank constraints
Original question and proposer: Yulia Alexandr and Guido Montúfar (Problem 35 and Theorem 34)
Proposed result: Integer simplex grids on rational subspaces generate the entire single-combination rank ideal. Linear algebra selects its contribution to the minimal pattern-ideal generators.

Title: A finite-witness test for oracle-free sound coverage
Original question and proposer: Xiaoyu Li, Andi Han, Dai Shi, Zheng Gao, Jiaojiao Jiang and Junbin Gao (§5, open problem 5)
Proposed result: Finite positive witnesses characterize when full positive data suffice to cover every unseen target point while remaining inside an unknown ambient language.

Title: A fourth Fourier mode rules out a proposed attention equilibrium density
Original question and proposer: Martin Burger, Samira Kabri, Yury Korolev, Tim Roith and Lukas Weigand (Section 5.2, equation (5.8))
Proposed result: For small nonzero anisotropy the proposed family cannot match the equilibrium to second order. An exact fourth-harmonic obstruction rules out every choice of its scalar parameter.

Title: A geometric criterion for scale-independent uniform generation
Original question and proposer: Jiaxun Li, Vinod Raman and Ambuj Tewari (§5, geometry beyond doubling)
Proposed result: On unbounded separable spaces, a uniform covering bound for each pair of fixed radii characterizes scale independence of uniform generation for classes with unbounded supports.

Title: A logarithmic gap between empirical risk minimizers under label symmetry
Original question and proposer: Amit Daniely, Sivan Sabato, Shai Ben-David and Shai Shalev-Shwartz (Question 16; sharpened in JMLR 2015, Question 19) · JMLR, Question 19
Proposed result: Two proper empirical risk minimizers on one label-symmetric class have realizable sample complexities differing by a factor logarithmic in the Natarajan dimension.

Title: A membership oracle cannot generate an unseen isolated real
Original question and proposer: Jiaxun Li, Vinod Raman and Ambuj Tewari (Appendix E, point-query access)
Proposed result: On the real line, adaptive membership and finite-sample ERM value queries can fail on every round even when a single closed target is exhaustively enumerated.

Title: A process criterion for universal multiclass online learning
Original question and proposer: Steve Hanneke and Hongao Wang (Appendix D.1, Q1)
Proposed result: Weighted tests on shared histories characterize learning with infinitely many labels. On a fixed process, sparse corruptions can drive regret to one even when realizable mistakes grow arbitrarily slowly.

Title: A semicircle profile for the cold deep linear singular-value gas
Original question and proposer: GitHub contributor garry-gum, extending Govind Menon (Problem 2(b), finite-depth concentration and profile)
Proposed result: At every finite depth, each continuum equilibrium concentrates at the predicted point. The rescaled end-to-end singular values have a semicircle law with an explicit depth-dependent variance.

Title: A successful regularizer with infinite selected disagreement dimension
Original question and proposer: Julian Asilis, Shaddin Dughmi, Vatsal Sharan, Alec Sun, Shang-Hua Teng and Chang Wang (question before Proposition 5.10)
Proposed result: A fixed regularizer PAC learns even though hypotheses it actually selects can shatter arbitrarily large sets of disagreements with one target.

Title: A test for representative generation with overlapping groups
Original question and proposer: Charlotte Peale, Vinod Raman and Omer Reingold (discussion of overlapping groups)
Proposed result: Convex hulls of fresh group-membership vectors characterize uniform and nonuniform representative generation with overlapping groups.

Title: An exponential gap between activation rank and polynomial Jacobian rank
Original question and proposer: J. Elisenda Grigsby and Kathryn Lindsey (Question 7.5 and Proposition 7.4)
Proposed result: Width-two ReLU networks with $L$ hidden layers have batches of activation rank $2^L$, while their polynomial Jacobians have at most $4L+1$ independent rows after accounting for rescaling symmetries.

Title: An unattained zero training loss for a scalar deep ReLU network
Original question and proposer: Eloi Martinet and Leon Bungert (Section 5, finite-data question and equation (10))
Proposed result: A scalar network with hidden widths one and two has squared-loss infimum zero on 30 rational examples. No weights interpolate the examples.

Title: An unbounded compactness gap for agnostic transductive learning
Original question and proposer: Julian Asilis, Siddartha Devic, Shaddin Dughmi, Vatsal Sharan and Shang-Hua Teng (§§3.3–4)
Proposed result: Every finite projection has vanishing excess error at a common rate, yet the full class has excess error one at every sample size. The first possible density for this failure is $\aleph_\omega$.

Title: Binary bandit learnability and the continuum hypothesis
Original question and proposer: Steve Hanneke and Liu Yang (§7, decidability of binary bandit learnability)
Proposed result: For an explicit class of binary rewards with open winning sets, learnability is equivalent over ZFC to the failure of the continuum hypothesis.

Title: Continuous onset can coexist with other stationary attention states
Original question and proposer: Kyunghoo Mun and Matthew Rosenzweig (Remark 2.4)
Proposed result: A smooth positive-semidefinite kernel on the circle has a continuous transition and a nonuniform stationary density strictly inside the conjectured uniqueness interval.

Title: Contrastive generation without compatible positive witnesses
Original question and proposer: Xiaoyu Li, Andi Han, Jiaojiao Jiang and Junbin Gao (§8(i) and Definition 6.21)
Proposed result: A countable class admits a generator that uses only the observed edge set, yet defeats every assignment of the proposed finite positive witnesses.

Title: Deciding efficient generation for pairs of deterministic context-free languages
Original question and proposer: Xiaoyu Li, Andi Han, Dai Shi, Jiaojiao Jiang and Junbin Gao (§5.2, hardness for natural classes and efficient closure generation)
Proposed result: Even for two deterministic context-free languages with infinite intersection, deciding whether a polynomial-time generator has a finite uniform expected mistake bound is Σ⁰₂-complete. The deterministic zero-mistake question has the same degree.

Title: Deciding uniform closedness of sparse ReLU networks
Original question and proposer: Quoc-Tung Le, Elisa Riccietti and Rémi Gribonval (Section 3.3 and the cube model of Section 4)
Proposed result: A finite real-algebraic procedure decides uniform closedness on a cube at arbitrary depth. A missing limit can be chosen piecewise affine with real algebraic data.

Title: Dense set-valued generation under bounded displacement
Original question and proposer: Anay Mehrotra, Grigoris Velegkas, Xifan Yu and Felix Zhou (after Theorem 7.8 in the preprint, after Theorem 39 at COLT 2026)
Proposed result: A finite-witness condition characterizes all attainable lower-density guarantees on full noiseless enumerations, including target-specific guarantees.

Title: Distribution-free identification from random unoriented pairs
Original question and proposer: Xiaoyu Li, Andi Han, Jiaojiao Jiang and Junbin Gao (§8(iv) and Appendix D.4, distribution-free iid pairs)
Proposed result: With arbitrary iid pair laws covering every positive, identification in probability is equivalent to almost-sure and clean adversarial identification.

Title: EMX learnability without bounded monotone compression
Original question and proposer: Shai Ben-David, Pavel Hrubeš, Shay Moran, Amir Shpilka and Amir Yehudayoff (§7, Question 1)
Proposed result: A countable family of finite sets is properly EMX-learnable, yet compressing samples of length up to m takes asymptotically log₂ m sample entries.

Title: Exact representability of two ReLU activation blocks
Original question and proposer: Yulia Alexandr, Moritz Grillo, Thiago Holleben, Guido Montúfar and Teresa Yu (Section 2.2, criterion after Proposition 4)
Proposed result: A finite linear-algebra test decides exact membership, including at boundary points. For rational block data, complex representability already gives rational factors.

Title: Exactly which error allowances an effective generator can use
Original question and proposer: Xiaoyu Li, Andi Han, Dai Shi, Zheng Gao, Jiaojiao Jiang and Junbin Gao (§5, computational versions of the nested-family dichotomy)
Proposed result: The high-coverage outcome on the canonical nested family is attainable effectively exactly when the allowed error count dominates a computable unbounded schedule.

Title: Finite determination of generic local ReLU realization fibers
Original question and proposer: J. Elisenda Grigsby, Kathryn Lindsey and David Rolnick (Section 2, functional-dimension conjecture and Lemma F.6)
Proposed result: Near almost every parameter, a finite batch determines agreement on the entire input space. The local fiber dimension is the number of parameters minus the functional dimension.

Title: Finite evidence for computable universal online learning
Original question and proposer: Dariusz Kalociński and Tomasz Steifer (§3)
Proposed result: Finite evidence characterizes learnability for arbitrary classes and the exact uniform mistake budget. Finding a defeating stream can require computing a path through any prescribed recursive tree.

Title: Finite Gaussian moments determine an entire ReLU function
Original question and proposer: Moritz Grillo and Guido Montúfar (Section 7, question 4)
Proposed result: For every fixed ReLU architecture, finitely many ordinary mixed Gaussian or product-Laplace moments determine its output everywhere. Almost every list of 2P+1 polynomial measurements suffices for P scalar-network parameters.

Title: Finite local identification of opposite ReLU neuron pairs
Original question and proposer: Pierre Stock and Rémi Gribonval (Section 5.4 before Lemma 16, paper first posted in 2021)
Proposed result: With free biases, the opposite pairs admit finite local identification exactly when their normals are independent across pairs and their two output vectors are independent within each pair.

Title: Generic and transversal ReLU parameters need not form an open set
Original question and proposer: J. Elisenda Grigsby, Kathryn Lindsey, Robert Meyerhoff and Chenxi Wu (Conjecture following Lemma 5.6)
Proposed result: A curve of layer-generic parameters fails transversality at vertices escaping to infinity and converges to a generic, transversal parameter.

Title: Generic combinatorial stability of deep ReLU networks
Original question and proposer: J. Elisenda Grigsby, Kathryn Lindsey, Robert Meyerhoff and Chenxi Wu (Section 5.2 and Definition 5.3)
Proposed result: At almost every choice of weights and biases, small perturbations preserve the entire labeled activation complex up to a continuously varying homeomorphism.

Title: Generic finite witnesses for nonclosed sparse ReLU matrix-product models
Original question and proposer: Quoc-Tung Le, Elisa Riccietti and Rémi Gribonval (Section 3.2, question following Lemma 3.2 and Figure 1)
Proposed result: For a fixed missing limit matrix, almost every tuple of more inputs than free parameters witnesses nonattainment. A larger generic tuple works for every such matrix at once.

Title: How small can the privacy budget be for language identification?
Original question and proposer: Xiaoyu Li, Andi Han, Jiaojiao Jiang and Junbin Gao (Appendix H.1, question 3)
Proposed result: For any diverging sublinear target exponent $r(n)$, every countable class admits that identification rate exactly when $n\varepsilon_n/r(n)$ tends to infinity.

Title: Identifying a cut when honest progress outpaces corruption
Original question and proposer: Xiaoyu Li, Andi Han, Jiaojiao Jiang and Junbin Gao (§8(iii) and Proposition 7.11)
Proposed result: A countable class of at least two infinite supports permits identification under diverging honest progress minus corruption exactly when its holes are finite and pairwise disjoint.

Title: Identifying languages under bounded displacement
Original question and proposer: Anay Mehrotra, Grigoris Velegkas, Xifan Yu and Felix Zhou (question before Theorem 7.6, published before Theorem 37 at COLT 2026)
Proposed result: Finite witnesses characterize exactly which countable language families can be identified from full, noiseless enumerations of bounded displacement.

Title: Infinite quotient fibers in width-one ReLU chains
Original question and proposer: Moritz Grillo and Guido Montúfar (Conjecture 1, both clauses)
Proposed result: Every realized function in a chain of at least three scalar hidden layers has uncountably many inequivalent parameterizations, resolving both clauses of Conjecture 1.

Title: Intersection signatures and effective resistance are incomparable
Original question and proposer: Hoang Anh Duy Le, Shaochen Zhong, Jerry Xiao, Jiamu Zhang, Yu-Neng Chuang, Li Li, Rui Chen, Shuai Xu, Zirui Liu, Kaixiong Zhou, Ning Xie, Vipin Chaudhary, Xia Hu and Zhaozhuo Xu (Appendix C, following Theorem C.1(2))
Proposed result: Cones over one cycle and over two shorter cycles have matching full-radius intersection signatures through every refinement round. Their effective resistances separate them in one round.

Title: Lists and finite partitions in uniform language generation
Original question and proposer: Moses Charikar, Chirag Pabbaraju and Ambuj Tewari (§5)
Proposed result: Two guesses suffice after one example, yet every finite partition has a part that defeats single-word generation. A Ramsey construction gives the separation at every list length.

Title: No fixed palette distinguishes all comparable languages by prefix traces
Original question and proposer: Moses Charikar, Jon Kleinberg and Chirag Pabbaraju (§6, lower bounds for the distinguishable coloring condition)
Proposed result: The strong trace condition requires arbitrarily many colors as alphabet size grows, already for finite collections of languages containing only one-letter words.

Title: Nonattainment of robust population risk by continuous ReLU predictors
Original question and proposer: Eloi Martinet and Leon Bungert (Section 5, existence for the adversarial objectives of Lunk et al.)
Proposed result: Two ReLU units approach the exact minimum robust absolute loss. Every continuous predictor misses it, in every dimension and for a range of perturbation radii.

Title: Nonclosed ReLU realization spaces at arbitrary depth
Original question and proposer: Eloi Martinet and Leon Bungert (Remark 3.11)
Proposed result: At every hidden depth of at least two, one fixed architecture has a limit outside its realization space, both uniformly on a rectangle and in every finite-p first-order Sobolev norm.

Title: Private generation in the limit on uncountable collections
Original question and proposer: Anay Mehrotra, Grigoris Velegkas, Xifan Yu and Felix Zhou (uncountable collections in §5)
Proposed result: One observation suffices for ordinary uniform generation, yet pure privacy can drive worst-case eventual success to zero. For a second collection, optimal success equals the additive privacy allowance.

Title: Private generation without a public witness bound
Original question and proposer: Xiaoyu Li, Andi Han, Jiaojiao Jiang and Junbin Gao (Appendix H.1, question 1)
Proposed result: For finite families, an infinite common intersection characterizes exponential private generation. For countable families a local condition on finite lists of strings is necessary and sufficient.

Title: Private list learning can fail at both dimensions one
Original question and proposer: Steve Hanneke, Shay Moran, Hilla Schefler and Iska Tsubari
Proposed result: Both proposed dimensions can equal one and an online learner can make at most one mistake, yet a differentially private learner can still need every label in its list.

Title: Prompted language generation by label fibers
Original question and proposer: Jiaxun Li, Vinod Raman and Ambuj Tewari (Questions 6.4–6.5, published as Questions 51–52 at COLT 2025)
Proposed result: A separate finite-witness condition for each label characterizes prompted generation. Every countable class works even for infinitely many prompts.

Title: Relative densities of abelian compression dictionaries
Original question and proposer: Xiaoyu Li, Andi Han, Dai Shi, Zheng Gao, Jiaojiao Jiang and Junbin Gao (§5, open problem 2)
Proposed result: Each deeper dictionary language has density zero in its predecessor. Partial enumeration of any positive-density core eventually identifies the target.

Title: Removing order and repetition counts from contrastive generation
Original question and proposer: Xiaoyu Li, Andi Han, Jiaojiao Jiang and Junbin Gao (Appendix D.3, order dependence)
Proposed result: Every successful generator on a countable contrastive class can use only the set of observed pairs. Finite witnesses indexed by admissible edge sets characterize success.

Title: Resistance-distance graph transformers can miss bipartiteness
Original question and proposer: Bohang Zhang, Shengjie Luo, Liwei Wang and Di He (Section 6 (ICLR 2023; first posted in 2022))
Proposed result: Two connected graphs have identical resistance-refinement colors at every depth. One is bipartite and the other contains triangles. Shortest-path refinement and their Laplacian spectra both distinguish them.

Title: Simultaneous noisy mistake and last-mistake bounds for finite language classes
Original question and proposer: Jon Kleinberg, Charlotte Peale and Omer Reingold (§§7.1 and 8, finite-class noisy guarantees)
Proposed result: One generator retains the finite-class noisy mistake bound at every horizon and has a bounded time of last mistake for every unknown finite noise budget.

Title: Stable graph refinement without a homomorphism-count characterization
Original question and proposer: Bohang Zhang, Jingchu Gai, Yiheng Du, Qiwei Ye, Di He and Liwei Wang (Appendices B and F.1)
Proposed result: A local update that caps neighbor counts has no such characterization, even on connected graphs. A second counterexample retains all neighbor multiplicities after local triangle initialization.

Title: The best finite-class rate for spherical cross-entropy
Original question and proposer: Jianfeng Lu and Stefan Steinerberger (Section 1.3, question before Theorem 5)
Proposed result: The negative logarithm of the optimal loss gap has order N to the power 1/s times log N on a sphere of intrinsic dimension s. The same rate corrects the pair-energy bound printed in Theorem 5 of arXiv v2.

Title: The closure dimension for corrupted contrastive pairs
Original question and proposer: Xiaoyu Li, Andi Han, Jiaojiao Jiang and Junbin Gao (§8(ii), with the unknown-budget example of Appendix D.2 discussed separately)
Proposed result: A deletion-based dimension gives the exact uniform distinct-pair threshold at every finite corruption budget and characterizes nonuniform generation by increasing unions.

Title: The clustering threshold for sharply concentrated noisy attention
Original question and proposer: Kyunghoo Mun and Matthew Rosenzweig (equations (1.18) and (1.19))
Proposed result: The threshold has the predicted logarithmic and log-log terms and the stated additive constant in every fixed dimension. Every nonuniform equilibrium minimizing the free energy at coexistence has a Gaussian profile after centering and rescaling.

Title: The computational strength of robust contrastive tell-tales
Original question and proposer: Xiaoyu Li, Andi Han, Jiaojiao Jiang and Junbin Gao (§8(v) and Appendix D.5)
Proposed result: The halting oracle suffices to return completed robust tell-tales and can be necessary even with decidable finite-sample consistency.

Title: The cone-sign conjecture for two ReLU neurons
Original question and proposer: Yuandong Tian (ICML, Conjecture 1 and the question after Theorem 4)
Proposed result: The residual has the predicted sign for every student opening. Noncollinear positive-loss strict saddles with exactly one teacher inside exist at every opening.

Title: The exact limiting rank in Gaussian attention
Original question and proposer: Castin, Ablin, Carrillo and Peyré (Section 4.5, Figures 4 and 11)
Proposed result: For opposite keys and queries, every bounded trajectory with a hyperbolic value matrix converges. Its limiting image is precisely the kernel of the key map.

Title: The Gaussian initialization law for depth-two diagonal completion
Original question and proposer: Rodrigo Treviño (Section 12.3, depth-two endpoint law)
Proposed result: A normalized-row Gram formula gives the endpoint limit in arbitrary width under a nonvanishing condition. In width two it gives an explicit continuous law for positive determinant and two equiprobable atoms for negative determinant.

Title: The halting threshold for prompted language generation
Original question and proposer: Jon Kleinberg and Sendhil Mullainathan (§7.2)
Proposed result: Two polynomial-time-checkable languages already require a halting oracle for eventual prompt completion. A bound on answer length characterizes the countable families that admit a generator.

Title: The homomorphism counts determined by shortest-path graph refinement
Original question and proposer: Bohang Zhang, Jingchu Gai, Yiheng Du, Qiwei Ye, Di He and Liwei Wang (Appendix B and Definition 3.1)
Proposed result: Shortest-path refinement counts exactly the forests, yet distinguishes connected graphs agreeing on every forest count. No ordinary homomorphism family represents it.

Title: The loss normalization in a ReLU curvature conjecture
Original question and proposer: Itay Safran, Gilad Yehudai and Ohad Shamir (COLT 2021, Conjecture 12 and equations (2) and (5))
Proposed result: The bound holds for the squared loss printed in equation (2). Arbitrarily close to a regular minimum, an explicit rotation violates it for the half-squared loss used by the displayed Hessian.

Title: The null space of full vertex-deletion constraints in graph networks
Original question and proposer: Niloofar Azizi, Nils M. Kriege and Horst Bischof (original full-deck proposal, later arXiv v1 discussion)
Proposed result: The surviving dimension is exactly the number of bipartite components for degree-weighted cards. On connected nonbipartite graphs the constrained unit sphere is empty, including for almost every large uniformly random labeled graph.

Title: The point-mass conjecture for deep linear spectral equilibrium
Original question and proposer: Alan Chen, Tejas S. Kotwal and Govind Menon (Section 8.3, equations (8.4) to (8.6))
Proposed result: The point mass is the unique minimizer and the only law satisfying the equilibrium force equation. For quadratic loss, the excess energy bounds the mean squared distance from that point.

Title: The quadratic threshold gap at tricritical noisy attention
Original question and proposer: Kyunghoo Mun and Matthew Rosenzweig (equation (1.17))
Proposed result: The critical couplings separate quadratically in every fixed dimension. A positive sixth-order coefficient determines the leading constant and forces the global minimizers onto the predicted local branch.

Title: The sharp separation exponent for smooth neural set encoders
Original question and proposer: Yair Davidson and Nadav Dym (Theorem 3.3 and Section 7, ICLR 2025)
Proposed result: On multisets of size at most n the optimal lower-Hölder exponent is n for Gaussian, tanh, sigmoid and softplus features on compact domains containing a line segment. The argument gives a finite upper exponent for deep smooth message passing.

Title: The singleton sparse-core density game
Original question and proposer: Xiaoyu Li, Andi Han, Dai Shi, Zheng Gao, Jiaojiao Jiang and Junbin Gao (§5, open problem 1)
Proposed result: For a known target and an unknown core of exact density $a$ up to one half, the optimal output density is $1-a$. Prescribing only lower density changes the answer.

Title: Total variation in representative language generation
Original question and proposer: Charlotte Peale, Vinod Raman and Omer Reingold (discussion of alternative distances)
Proposed result: For countable partitions and countable target families, total-variation representative generation in the limit has an exact finite-exception criterion for each target.

Title: Unbounded deep linear completion trajectories escape in norm
Original question and proposer: Rodrigo Treviño (Section 12.4, question 1)
Proposed result: Every unbounded trajectory eventually leaves every bounded set. The result holds in all widths in the original finite-temperature model, so almost every full-rank initialization escapes in norm.

Title: Uniform generation from all state-bounded binary automata
Original question and proposer: Marcelo Arenas, Pablo Barceló, Luis Cofré and Alexander Kozachinskiy (question following Theorem 4.2 in the ICML paper)
Proposed result: For the full class of infinite binary languages recognized by at most $s$ states, the worst-case uniform sample complexity $T(s)$ satisfies $\log_2\log_2\log_2 T(s)=\Theta(s\log s)$.

Title: Universal monotone set networks on infinite ground sets
Original question and proposer: Soutrik Sarangi, Yonatan Sverdlov, Nadav Dym and Abir De (Section 7 and Theorem 14 (NeurIPS 2025))
Proposed result: Triangular-hat sums and monotone decoders uniformly approximate every continuous inclusion-monotone target on bounded-size multisets over a compact ground set. A single countable bank suffices and fixed finite banks cannot serve every target.

Title: What shortest paths and resistance can count together
Original question and proposer: Bohang Zhang, Jingchu Gai, Yiheng Du, Qiwei Ye, Di He and Liwei Wang (Appendix B, other architectures)
Proposed result: The joint graph transformer counts exactly forests. For every cyclic pattern there are two connected diameter-two graphs it cannot distinguish, even though their counts differ.

Title: When a width-one network attains its best fit
Original question and proposer: Lek-Heng Lim, Mateusz Michałek and Yang Qi (two questions after Theorem 5 in the 2022 journal version)
Proposed result: Vector-output tanh chains of every hidden depth can fail to attain the least-squares infimum on an open set of labels. Width-one ReLU chains attain a best fit on every finite sample.

Title: When does an overwide matrix factorization have intrinsic training dynamics?
Original question and proposer: Sibylle Marcotte, Gabriel Peyré and Rémi Gribonval (following Theorem 3.9 (ICLR 2026))
Proposed result: A single matrix rank test decides whether training from a fixed initialization admits a product-dependent gradient metric. Failure can already be witnessed with smooth autonomous losses.

Title: When random sparse ReLU networks have no best fit
Original question and proposer: Quoc-Tung Le, Elisa Riccietti and Rémi Gribonval (Question 3.2 (NeurIPS 2023))
Proposed result: For independent masks of bounded expected degree, the probability that some nine-example ReLU problem has no minimizer tends to one. The linear matrix-product test has a different, explicit Poisson limit.

Title: When the previous guess cannot remember a language
Original question and proposer: Jon Kleinberg, Anay Mehrotra, Amin Saberi and Grigoris Velegkas (§1.3)
Proposed result: A nested family of regular languages with singleton telltales defeats every last-guess learner, even on repetition-free texts. One extra bit restores exact identification.

Title: When vanishing noise permits a target-dependent mistake budget
Original question and proposer: Jon Kleinberg, Charlotte Peale and Omer Reingold (§7.1, bounded mistakes under vanishing noise)
Proposed result: Countable classes admit a target-dependent mistake cap on every vanishing-noise stream exactly when all finite intersections of targets are infinite.

Title: Which conservation laws survive in deep linear networks?
Original question and proposer: Sibylle Marcotte, Rémi Gribonval and Gabriel Peyré (Section 4, following Proposition 4.1 (NeurIPS 2023))
Proposed result: Additional local laws exist with scalar input and output and wide hidden layers. For square layers of any width and depth, the balance matrices generate every smooth local law at generic weights.

Title: Which language collections attain Pareto-optimal generation times?
Original question and proposer: Moses Charikar and Chirag Pabbaraju (introduction and §§3.3–3.4)
Proposed result: A well-order test characterizes exactly which countable collections attain Pareto-optimal generation times and recovers every attainable optimal profile in the unrestricted model.

Title: Which languages can a private learner identify in the limit?
Original question and proposer: Anay Mehrotra, Grigoris Velegkas, Xifan Yu and Felix Zhou (source of the gap between Thms. 1.5 and C.5)
Proposed result: For a countable family of infinite languages presented without repetition, private identification is possible exactly when every two distinct languages share only finitely many words.

Title: A bounded rank test for separators in permutation-packing posets
Original question and proposer: Natasha Blitvić, Mohammed Slim Kammoun and Einar Steingrímsson (§7, item 5)
Proposed result: At overlap $m$, the answer for any number of copies is determined by testing up to $6(m+1)+1$ copies.

Title: A finite automaton for bounded jumps and arbitrary forbidden permutation patterns
Original question and proposer: Nathaniel Nadler (§9.2)
Proposed result: Every finite forbidden set has a finite-state counting algorithm and a rational generating function for each fixed jump bound.

Title: A packing-preserving lift and uniform Catalan representatives
Original question and proposer: Natasha Blitvić, Mohammed Slim Kammoun and Einar Steingrímsson (§7, item 6, Catalan part)
Proposed result: A count-preserving lift gives Catalan representatives for every overlap $m\ge 3$ and length $K\ge 2m$.

Title: Adjacent jumps in 123-avoiding permutations at fixed and growing radii
Original question and proposer: Nathaniel Nadler (§9.4)
Proposed result: For 123-avoiders, the fixed-radius growth deficit is asymptotic to $16\pi^2/m^2$. A Brownian excursion maximum gives the surviving fraction when the radius grows with length.

Title: An atomic permutation class without a growth rate
Original question and proposer: Jay Pantone and Vincent Vatter (Question 2.6)
Proposed result: Every pair of patterns in this class occurs together in a third, yet its upper and lower exponential growth rates differ.

Title: Every positive integer power sequence occurs in permutation packing
Original question and proposer: Natasha Blitvić, Mohammed Slim Kammoun and Einar Steingrímsson (§7, item 9)
Proposed result: Every positive integer base occurs for infinitely many patterns with overlap two.

Title: Exactly when variable-overlap permutation packings factor
Original question and proposer: Natasha Blitvić, Mohammed Slim Kammoun and Einar Steingrímsson (§7, item 2)
Proposed result: A finite criterion decides whether counts split at a designated overlap and gives a witness whenever they fail to split.

Title: No universal cutoff for prescribed consecutive-pattern packings
Original question and proposer: Natasha Blitvić, Mohammed Slim Kammoun and Einar Steingrímsson (§7, item 8)
Proposed result: Two patterns can have arbitrarily many initial packing counts in common and differ at the very next count.

Title: Telescoping certificates for Foatic permutation actions
Original question and proposer: Peter Mao (Section 7, Table 4)
Proposed result: The certificates in all thirteen rows hold. The proofs use corner entries of permutation diagrams, descents of cycle words and a record-preservation identity.

Title: Which permutation pattern counts are homomesic under Lehmer rotation?
Original question and proposer: Jennifer Elder, Nadia Lafrenière, Erin McNicholas, Jessica Striker and Amanda Welch (Problem 4.36, added in the March 2023 revision)
Proposed result: The classification covers ordinary patterns, required position adjacencies and either endpoint anchor. No pattern of length at least four qualifies. At length three, the possible bonds depend on whether the pattern is monotone.

Title: Affine compactness and 2-SAT without choice
Original question and proposer: Anthony Li, Ishin Shan, Matthew Snodgrass, Riley Thornton and Rui Zhou (after Thm. 5)
Proposed result: In one model of pure ZF, compactness holds for affine equations over all finite abelian groups and fails for 2-SAT. This completes the Boolean implication diagram.

Title: An ideal realizes all analytic limit sets without the proposed scheme
Original question and proposer: Rafał Filipów, Adam Kwela and Paolo Leonetti (Question 9.2).
Proposed result: A coanalytic ideal realizes precisely the analytic sets as ideal limit sets in every uncountable Polish space, although every candidate tree fails the proposed scheme condition.

Title: An ideal that is its own set of ideal limit points
Original question and proposer: Rafał Filipów, Adam Kwela and Paolo Leonetti (Question 10.11).
Proposed result: For any injective enumeration of a countable dense subset of Cantor space, a proper ideal on the natural numbers is exactly the set of its own ideal limit points for that sequence.

Title: An infinite poset with no infinite chain or antichain in the finite partition model
Original question and proposer: Amitayu Banerjee (order and Ramsey parts of Question 8.1 in v1, later Question 7.1)
Proposed result: In Bruce’s model, subsets of the atoms modulo finite changes form an infinite poset with no infinite chain or antichain. Comparability gives a two-coloring with no infinite homogeneous set.

Title: Antichains in locally finite trees without countable choice
Original question and proposer: Amitayu Banerjee and Alexa Gopaulsingh (Q6.6 and Q6.7)
Proposed result: Every uncountable locally finite rooted tree can have an uncountable antichain, even when a sequence of pairs has no choice function in pure ZF.

Title: Arithmetic progressions in the image of an infinite clique
Original question and proposer: Rafał Filipów, Krzysztof Kowitz and Adam Kwela (Q1.2) and their unified paper (Q7.8 and the Ramsey clause of Q16.6).
Proposed result: An infinite clique can be thinned so its real edge labels avoid every relation in a prescribed finite list of invariant three-term equations. Two Katětov comparisons fail.

Title: Canonical pairs and higher-arity Ramsey finiteness
Original question and proposer: Brinda Venkataramani (Q8.1, using arity in the sense of Brot, Cao and Fernández-Bretón).
Proposed result: Pair Ramsey finiteness implies canonical pair finiteness. At higher arity neither implication is provable in ZF. Strict inclusion in one model is possible at every arity.

Title: Cardinal comparability and choice at the first uncountable ordinal
Original question and proposer: Paul Howard and Eleftherios Tachtsis (§8, Q4)
Proposed result: In one model of ZF, every uncountable set contains a copy of ω₁, yet some ω₁-indexed family of finite sets has no choice function.

Title: Dense presentations of the basic Fraenkel model
Original question and proposer: Brian Pinsky (§5, Conjecture 13 in the arXiv version)
Proposed result: Frucht's theorem can fail in a permutation model even when the presenting group has no nonidentity internal permutation. The proposed converse holds for closed groups with finite supports.

Title: Egorov ideals on arbitrary finite measure spaces
Original question and proposer: Adam Kwela (paragraph before Theorem 3.4 and Remark 6.10).
Proposed result: For Egorov ideals tested on arbitrary finite measures, one fixed exceptional fraction suffices. Fubini sums with analytic row ideals obey the same criterion as on the unit interval.

Title: Every infinite set splits in the finite partition model
Original question and proposer: Benjamin Baker Bruce (finite partition model, recorded explicitly as open by Brinda Venkataramani in 2026)
Proposed result: At every rank in Bruce’s model, each infinite set splits into two infinite subsets. This rules out amorphous sets even though infinite Dedekind-finite sets exist there.

Title: Finite choice implies Frucht's theorem
Original question and proposer: Brian Pinsky (Appendix 6.1, five weak-choice implications)
Proposed result: Choice for families of nonempty finite sets suffices to realize every group as the automorphism group of a simple graph in ZFA. All five implications in Pinsky’s list follow.

Title: Finite Ramsey homogeneity lowers arity without choice
Original question and proposer: Joshua Brot, Mengyang Cao and David Fernández-Bretón (Q5.1(2) and (3) in the final version).
Proposed result: In ZF, Ramsey finiteness propagates to every higher arity on arbitrary sets. Two-summand Boolean Hindman finiteness then implies Ramsey finiteness at each arity of at least two.

Title: Finite symmetries of binary relations on amorphous sets
Original question and proposer: Paul Howard and Eleftherios Tachtsis (§6, Problem 3)
Proposed result: Every finite list of binary relations on an amorphous set has a common nonidentity involution of finite support, even after naming any finite set of points. Both rigidity principles in Problem 3 exclude amorphous sets.

Title: Frucht's theorem and weak forms of anti-foundation
Original question and proposer: Junhong Chen and Daheng Ju (§§7–8, the three implications in the second open question)
Proposed result: Over ZF without Foundation, Frucht's theorem is equivalent to all three weak representation principles CWFAFA₂, WFAFA₂ and WFAFA′₂.

Title: Hajnal’s product theorem without the ultrafilter lemma
Original question and proposer: Amitayu Banerjee and Zalán Gyenis (Q3.2 in v1, later Q5.2). Amitayu Banerjee restated it and asked about choice for pairs in 2021
Proposed result: One model satisfies every finite-color product theorem while choice for pairs fails. In pure ZF with dependent choice, two countably chromatic graphs can have a bipartite product.

Title: Hereditary differential compactness is the Ramsey property
Original question and proposer: Rafał Filipów, Krzysztof Kowitz and Adam Kwela (Q10.4(2a)). Krzysztof Kowitz and Jacek Tryba proved the sparse ideal comparison in 2025.
Proposed result: Hereditary differential compactness equals Ramsey compactness in ZFC. Under CH a compact separable Hausdorff space separates differential compactness from its hereditary version.

Title: Hereditary rigidity on the real line
Original question and proposer: Paul Howard and Eleftherios Tachtsis (§6, Problems 4 and 6)
Proposed result: Consistently with ZF and dependent choice, every binary relation on the reals has a countable restriction with a shift automorphism. Hereditary rigidity can fail to pass from a set to its power set.

Title: Integer weights and promise compactness without choice
Original question and proposer: Bertalan Bodor (Q6.3, Q6.5 and Q6.6)
Proposed result: Local exact-one satisfiability can give global not-all-equal colorings without choice for pairs. In a second example, a symmetric operation coexists with compactness equivalent to the ultrafilter lemma.

Title: No tall summable ideal is Katětov-homogeneous
Original question and proposer: Rafał Filipów, Krzysztof Kowitz and Adam Kwela (Q8.8(2) and Q10.4(1a)).
Proposed result: Every tall summable ideal has a positive restriction outside the required Katětov comparison. Under CH its compactness property can fail to be hereditary.

Title: One character sequence realizes complete Borel rank for every ideal
Original question and proposer: Paolo Leonetti (Q6.3). Adam Kwela asks about the general-domain upper bound.
Proposed result: One sequence of powers of two realizes a subgroup complete for the multiplicative Borel class of every Borel ideal, at every countable rank attained by an ideal.

Title: One family suffices for all interior densities
Original question and proposer: David Valderrama (Q4.2, both inequalities).
Proposed result: Any nonempty set of interior input densities gives the same reaping and permutation cardinals as the single density 1/2, with unrestricted permutation outputs.

Title: Ordered choice, Dilworth’s theorem and the Erdős–Dushnik–Miller principle
Original question and proposer: Eleftherios Tachtsis (§4). Amitayu Banerjee listed it as Q6.5 in 2021
Proposed result: Choice for linearly ordered families implies the finite-width Dilworth theorem in ZFA. The note also explains Tachtsis’s 2024 matching example. The score covers the Dilworth implication.

Title: Projective type and self-surjections of power sets
Original question and proposer: Yifan Hu, Ruihuan Mao and Guozhen Shen (§6, Questions 6.1 and 6.2, published in 2026)
Proposed result: For an amorphous set, some positive finite power of its power set admits a noninjective self-surjection exactly when the set is of projective type. In that case every positive finite power does.

Title: Promise reductions and partial assignments without finite choice
Original question and proposer: Bertalan Bodor (Q6.4)
Proposed result: A common algebraic reduction between promise constraint problems gives an implication between their compactness principles in ZF, even on sets with no linear order.

Title: Rado selection and the Boolean prime ideal theorem in ZF
Original question and proposer: Yehuda Rav identified the question as open in his review of the 1977 paper. Paul Howard and Eleftherios Tachtsis explicitly restated the pure-ZF question in 2014
Proposed result: Over pure ZF, Rado’s selection lemma is equivalent to the Boolean prime ideal theorem. In the presence of atoms, the draft identifies exactly which additional ordering principle suffices.

Title: Rainbow Ramsey for triples implies König’s lemma without choice
Original question and proposer: Amitayu Banerjee, Alexa Gopaulsingh and Zalán Molnár (Question 8.3).
Proposed result: Global rainbow Ramsey at every arity from three upward implies König’s lemma in ZF. For pairs with multiplicity at least three, König’s lemma is equivalent to countable choice for pairs under the rainbow hypothesis.

Title: Rainbow Ramsey witnesses and the Boolean prime ideal theorem
Original question and proposer: Amitayu Banerjee, Alexa Gopaulsingh and Zalán Molnár (Q8.2). Brinda Venkataramani (2026, Q7.15 and Q8.4).
Proposed result: The Boolean prime ideal theorem can hold while every finite-arity rainbow Ramsey principle fails. In a second ZF model, the permitted multiplicities and intersections of equal-colored sets give distinct finiteness classes.

Title: Random forcing and oscillation of asymptotic density
Original question and proposer: Christina Brech, Jörg Brendle and Márcio Telles (Q37 and Conjecture 41). David Valderrama posed the relative-density version in 2025 (Q4.4).
Proposed result: In the random model both oscillation cardinals equal ℵ₁ while the null covering number is ℵ₂. Adding one interior input density changes the permutation cardinal.

Title: Rigid relations on subsets of ordinal Cantor cubes
Original question and proposer: Paul Howard and Eleftherios Tachtsis (§6, Problem 5, following Hamkins’s 2009 question)
Proposed result: In ZF every subset of every ordinal-indexed binary cube has a rigid binary relation on its own points. The first Kinna–Wagner principle therefore implies the rigid relation principle.

Title: Rigidity need not descend from a power set
Original question and proposer: Paul Howard and Eleftherios Tachtsis (§6, Problem 7)
Proposed result: Relative to the consistency of ZF, an amorphous set can have a rigid power set while every binary relation on the underlying set has a nontrivial automorphism.

Title: The axiom of choice and distinguishing vertex colorings
Original question and proposer: Amitayu Banerjee, Zalán Molnár and Alexa Gopaulsingh (Q8.2(4, 8)). Marcin Stawiski restated part (4) in 2026
Proposed result: Over ZF, the axiom of choice is equivalent to the existence of a distinguishing chromatic number for every infinite connected graph, even when restricted to rigid graphs.

Title: The Erdős–Dushnik–Miller theorem and countable unions
Original question and proposer: Paul Howard and Eleftherios Tachtsis (§8, Q3)
Proposed result: Both forms of the Erdős–Dushnik–Miller theorem studied here can hold while a countable union of countably infinite sets is uncountable in pure ZF.

Title: The number of colors matters for Ramsey finiteness on a fixed set
Original question and proposer: Joshua Brot, Mengyang Cao and David Fernández-Bretón (Q5.1(5) in v1, Q5.1(4) in the final version).
Proposed result: In one ZF model each successive finite palette separates the local Ramsey properties for every arity from two upward and the local two-summand Boolean Hindman properties.

Title: The support test for ideal-characterized circle subgroups
Original question and proposer: Dikran Dikranjan, Pratulananda Das and Kumardipta Bose (§3). Rafał Filipów, Adam Kwela, Paolo Leonetti and Jacek Tryba restated the question in 2026 (Q2.19).
Proposed result: A single Bohr ideal characterizes failure of the whole-circle support test. Haar integration proves that the test holds for all nonpathological analytic P-ideals, including density zero.

Title: Three Boolean summands do not imply the full Hindman property in ZF
Original question and proposer: Joshua Brot and Mengyang Cao (p. 13). Joshua Brot, Mengyang Cao and David Fernández-Bretón (2019, Q5.1(1)).
Proposed result: In a model of ZF, every finite coloring admits an infinite family monochromatic for one-, two- and three-term Boolean sums, while the full Hindman property fails.

Title: Two prescribed targets for rearranging relative density
Original question and proposer: Christina Brech, Jörg Brendle and Márcio Telles (Q56). David Valderrama (2025, Q4.5).
Proposed result: A forcing extension has fewer than continuum many permutations that send every interior relative density to each of two prescribed interior targets.

Title: Uncountable partial choice and bounded countable families
Original question and proposer: Paul Howard and Eleftherios Tachtsis (§8, Q2)
Proposed result: If every uncountable family of nonempty finite sets admits choices on an uncountable subfamily, then every countable family of nonempty sets of uniformly bounded finite size has a choice function.

Title: Well-orderable unions in the countable partition model
Original question and proposer: Amitayu Banerjee (Question 8.4 in v1, later Question 7.2; remaining case posed by Brinda Venkataramani in Question 10.2 (2026))
Proposed result: A well-orderable family of well-orderable sets has a well-orderable union for every ambient number of atoms in the countable partition model.

Title: When measurable Dilworth decompositions exist
Original question and proposer: Bartłomiej Bosek, Jarosław Grytczuk and Zbigniew Lonc (Conj. 3)
Proposed result: A measurable poset of width two can have every measurable chain null. For perfect measures, countable separation on a conull set characterizes the existence of the optimal partition.

Title: Which fields have algebraic closures in the finite partition model?
Original question and proposer: Amitayu Banerjee (algebraic-closure part (Form 233) of Question 8.1 in v1, later Question 7.1)
Proposed result: A field in Bruce’s model has an algebraic closure exactly when its underlying set is well-orderable. Any two closures are isomorphic over the base field.
